one_liner: Pure-Rust dense (and sparse) linear algebra whose multithreaded QR and mid-size eigensolvers outrun OpenBLAS and Eigen; MKL still leads.
what_it_does: faer is a Rust crate with matrix types (Mat, MatRef, MatMut, Col, Row), operator-overloaded arithmetic and a LAPACK-scale set of factorizations: LLT, LDLT, LBLT (Bunch-Kaufman), LU with partial or full pivoting, QR with or without column pivoting, SVD, self-adjoint and general eigendecomposition, generalized EVD, plus sparse Cholesky/LU/QR and matrix-free eigen/SVD solvers. It has its own API, not the BLAS/LAPACK ABI: a high-level API on Mat, and a low-level API where the caller supplies scratch memory (dyn-stack) and the parallelism setting. An in-repo faer-ffi crate (cdylib, cbindgen) exposes the dense factorizations, matmul and triangular solves to C (faer.h) and C++17 (faer.hpp).
how_it_is_fast: Matrix multiplication follows the BLIS approach (packing plus register-blocked micro-kernels), with runtime CPU-feature dispatch to precompiled SIMD variants through the pulp crate, the gemm crate, nano-gemm for small products and, on x86-64 with std, the author's private-gemm-x86 backend (0.22 changelog: 'accelerated matrix multiply backend on x86_64'). Decompositions are blocked so most flops land in that GEMM; memory-bound phases (column-pivoted QR, full-pivot LU, reduction to bidiagonal/tridiagonal/Hessenberg form) use fused kernels that do A x and A^T y in one pass over A. Threading is Rayon (plus the spindle crate); SIMD for user scalar types deinterleaves AoS data to SoA in registers.
when_to_use: Rust code that needs dense factorizations (QR, LU, Cholesky, SVD, EVD) on medium-to-large matrices without linking a C/Fortran BLAS/LAPACK.
Multithreaded QR of large f64 matrices: the JOSS plots (i5-11400, 12 threads) put faer about 3x OpenBLAS and about 5x Eigen at n=10^4.
Eigendecomposition around n=1000, where the plots show faer ahead of OpenBLAS (about 2.2e9 vs 1.2e9 n^3/s).
Extended precision: faer ships a SIMD double-double type (fx128/cx128) and the plots show it several times faster than Eigen on f128 matmul and QR.
Projects that want one portable static binary (x86-64 and AArch64 NEON SIMD, no_std-capable core) instead of distributing OpenBLAS or MKL.
when_not_to_use: When Intel MKL is available on Intel hardware and only speed matters: the paper's plots show MKL ahead on QR and EVD and level on matmul.
Large eigendecompositions (n=10^4): the plots show faer behind OpenBLAS, BLIS and MKL (about 2.9e9 vs 3.7e9, 4.0e9 and 4.6e9 n^3/s).
Small fixed-size matrices (graphics, robotics, 3x3/4x4): the crate docs say its design is not well suited to that and point to nalgebra or cgmath.
Existing C/C++ or Fortran code that calls BLAS/LAPACK symbols: there is no drop-in ABI, and the C/C++ binding (faer-ffi) is not published on crates.io.

Ill-conditioned or singular inputs without your own checks: open bug reports show NaN from qr().solve_lstsq on a 1e16-conditioned 3x3 system (#265) and NaN instead of 0 from a singular 3x3 determinant on 0.23.2 (#260).

integration.form: crate (faer on crates.io); optional cdylib with C and C++ headers built from faer-ffi in the repo
integration.dependencies: pure Rust crates: pulp, gemm, nano-gemm, private-gemm-x86 (x86-64, std), dyn-stack, bytemuck, generativity, reborrow, equator, num-complex, num-traits, libm; optional rayon + spindle (default on), rand, npyz
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.84.0 (MSRV); nightly needed only for the AVX-512 'nightly' feature; faer.hpp needs C++17
integration.platforms: any Rust target; explicit SIMD on x86-64 (AVX2/FMA, AVX-512 with nightly) and AArch64 NEON; no SVE/SME/RVV kernels yet; an open issue (#255) reports matmul compile failure on i686-unknown-linux-gnu
integration.thread_safety: Rust ownership rules apply (MatRef is shareable, MatMut is exclusive); parallelism is a global setting (set_global_par/get_global_par) or a per-call Par argument in the low-level API
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — replaces LAPACK/OpenBLAS functionality for Rust callers through a different API; the C/C++ binding has its own function names (libfaer_v0_24_*), not BLAS/LAPACK symbols

gotchas: Development moved to codeberg.org/sarah-quinones/faer; the GitHub repo is a mirror, so file issues and track releases there (crate repository field points to Codeberg).
Pre-1.0 with frequent breaking changes: 0.20-0.21 was a full project refactor, 0.24 removed serde support, and the docs warn that eigenvalue order from Mat::eigen is unspecified and may change.

The checked-in faer-ffi/faer.h declares libfaer_v0_23_* functions while faer.hpp calls libfaer_v0_24_*; build.rs only regenerates the header when FAER_FFI is set, so build it yourself rather than copying the header.
The MIT crate carries ported code under other licences (COPYING.EIGEN.MPL2, COPYING.LAPACK.BSD and two SuiteSparse BSD notices in faer/), so keep those notices when vendoring.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick faer over Eigen when you are in Rust or need fast multithreaded large QR or mid-size eigensolvers (Eigen trails both faer and OpenBLAS in the paper's QR plot), and over OxiBLAS when you need full LAPACK-style decompositions rather than BLAS kernels; for matrices in the tens BLASFEO is the better fit.
verified_claims_summary: The JOSS 2023 paper (peer-reviewed software paper, DOI 10.21105/joss.06099) plots n^3/time for f64 matmul, QR and EVD on an Intel Core i5-11400 with 12 threads against OpenBLAS, BLIS, MKL and Eigen (built with -fopenmp); readings show about 3x OpenBLAS on QR at n=10^4, parity on large matmul, and a mid-size EVD win, while MKL stays ahead. No Rust toolchain, flags, library versions or benchmark code are given, and the plots date from November 2023, before the current 0.24 code.
status_note: Actively developed (crate 0.24.4 released 2026-06-24, about 4.8M crates.io downloads, last mirror commit 2026-09-04), MIT-licensed and used widely in the Rust ecosystem, but still pre-1.0 with open correctness bugs on ill-conditioned inputs.
